'''Robin Franklin''', FRS is a British cell biologist and neuroscientist. He is currently a Principal Investigator at [[Altos Labs]] Cambridge Institute of Science<ref>{{cite web |title=Robin Franklin |url=https://altoslabs.com/team/principal-investigators-cambridge/robin-franklin/ |website=Altos Labs |language=en}}</ref> having previously been Professor of
Stem Cell Medicine at the [[Wellcome–MRC Cambridge Stem Cell Institute]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Robin Franklin |url=https://www.stemcells.cam.ac.uk/people/pi/franklin |website=University of Cambridge |language=en |date=5 June 2019}}</ref>  He is Emeritus Fellow of [[Pembroke College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Robin Franklin |url=https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/college/master-and-fellows/list-fellows/professor-robin-franklin |website=Pembroke |language=en}}</ref>

== Education ==
Robin Franklin was educated at the [[Haberdashers' Aske's Boys' School|Haberdashers' Aske's School]], Elstree.<ref>{{cite web |title=Schoolboys from Haberdashers' Askes, Elstree, listed in Who's Who book |url=https://www.borehamwoodtimes.co.uk/news/11648164.schoolboys-from-haberdashers-askes-elstree-listed-in-whos-who-book/ |website=Borehamwood Times}}</ref> He was awarded a Bachelor of Science degree from [[University College London|UCL]] in 1985 and a Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine from the [[Royal Veterinary College]], [[University of London]] in 1988.<ref name=education>{{cite web |title=Robin Franklin |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/robin-franklin-35831/ |website=Royal Society}}</ref> He received his PhD in neuroscience from the University of Cambridge in 1992.<ref name=education />

== Research and career ==
Franklin is a pioneer in the biology of [[remyelination]], an area where he has made many seminal contributions. These include, 1) identifying the role of the innate immune response, 2) the effects of ageing and how these can be reversed, 3) the activation and plasticity of CNS stem cells following injury (including the origin of the remyelinating cells of the CNS), 4)
the transcriptional and epigenetic control of CNS stem cell differentiation; and 5) the first demonstrations of remyelination by transplanted [[oligodendrocyte progenitor cell]]s and [[olfactory ensheathing cell]]s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Diabetes drug could halt progression of multiple sclerosis, study suggests |url=https://www.ft.com/content/01157784-e6cb-11e9-b112-9624ec9edc59 |website=Financial Times |date=6 October 2019}}</ref> His studies on RXR and metformin in the context of CNS remyelination have led to clinical trials.<ref>{{cite web |title=Multiple Sclerosis could be reversed by activating stem cells in brain, study suggests |url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/Multiple-Sclerosis-could-be-reversed-by-activating-stem-cells-in-brain-study-suggests/article15583007.ece |website=The Hindu |language=en-IN |date=6 December 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Jha |first1=Alok |title=MS could be reversed by activating stem cells in brain, new study suggests |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2010/dec/05/ms-activating-stem-cells-brain |website=The Guardian |date=5 December 2010}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
*2006: Elected Fellow of [[Royal College of Pathologists]]
*2018: Elected Fellow of [[Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Fellowship Board |url=https://www.rcvs.org.uk/who-we-are/committees/advancement-of-the-professions-committee/fellowship-board/ |website=RCVS |language=en}}</ref>
*2016: Elected Fellow of [[Academy of Medical Sciences (United Kingdom)|Academy of Medical Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Robin Franklin |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/fellow/Robin%20Milroy%20James-Franklin-0033z00002qIIi0AAG |website=The Academy of Medical Sciences}}</ref>
*[[List of fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2022|2022: Elected Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Outstanding scientists elected as Fellows and Foreign Members of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2022/05/new-fellows-2022/ |website=Royal Society}}</ref>
*2004: Cavanagh Prize of the [[British Neuropathological Society]]<ref>{{cite web |title=The Cavanagh Prize Lecture |url=https://www.bns.org.uk/the-cavanagh-prize-lecture/ |website=BNS}}</ref>
*2017: Barancik Prize – International Prize for Research innovation, [[National Multiple Sclerosis Society]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Barancik Prize for Innovation in MS Research |url=https://www.nationalmssociety.org/For-Professionals/Researchers/Society-Funding/Special-Awards-and-Prizes-(1)/Barancik-Prize-for-Innovation-in-MS-Research |publisher=National Multiple Sclerosis Society}}</ref>
*2021: [[King Faisal Prize]] for Medicine<ref>{{cite web |last1=Puhl |first1=Laura |title=Professor Robin Franklin receives King Faisal Prize in Medicine |url=https://www.stemcells.cam.ac.uk/news/professor-robin-franklin-receives-king-faisal-prize-medicine |website=Stem Cell Institute |language=en |date=13 January 2022}}</ref>
